Appendix D: Common Error Messages

The ORA errors you will meet while learning, with the usual cause and the remedy. The full text and action for any message is in Oracle’s Database Error Messages reference.

ErrorMessageUsual causeRemedy
ORA-00001unique constraint violatedDuplicate keyUse a new key value or UPDATE the existing row
ORA-00054resource busy and acquire with NOWAIT specifiedAnother session holds a lockCOMMIT/ROLLBACK there, or wait
ORA-00060deadlock detectedTwo sessions wait for each otherLock rows in the same order; commit sooner
ORA-00904invalid identifierMisspelled column; alias used in WHERE; wrong table aliasCheck names; repeat the expression
ORA-00905 / ORA-00907missing keyword / right parenthesisIncomplete statementRe-read the syntax
ORA-00918column ambiguously definedSame column name in two joined tablesQualify with the table alias
ORA-00923FROM keyword not foundMissing comma or FROM; * with other columnsFix the select list
ORA-00933SQL command not properly endedUnsupported clause such as LIMIT; text after the statementUse FETCH FIRST; remove extra text
ORA-00934group function is not allowed hereAggregate in WHEREUse HAVING
ORA-00936missing expressionA trailing comma or operatorComplete the expression
ORA-00937not a single-group group functionPlain column with an aggregate and no GROUP BYAdd GROUP BY
ORA-00942table or view does not existTypo, wrong schema, no privilegeCheck owner and grants
ORA-00947not enough valuesINSERT value count differsList columns; match counts
ORA-00979not a GROUP BY expressionSelect-list column not in GROUP BYAdd it to GROUP BY or aggregate it
ORA-01400cannot insert NULLMandatory column omittedSupply a value
ORA-01402view WITH CHECK OPTION where-clause violationDML would make the row invisible in the viewChange the data or the view
ORA-01407cannot update to NULLNOT NULL column set to NULLProvide a value
ORA-01417 / ORA-01719(+) restrictionsOuter join to more than one table / (+) with OR or INUse ANSI joins
ORA-01427single-row subquery returns more than one row= with a multi-row subqueryUse IN, or restrict the subquery
ORA-01438value larger than specified precisionNUMBER(p,s) too smallWiden the column
ORA-01476divisor is equal to zeroDivision by 0Use NULLIF(x, 0)
ORA-01722invalid numberText converted to a numberCheck data and types; explicit conversion
ORA-01789 / ORA-01790incorrect number of result columns / datatype mismatchSet operator queries differAlign columns and types
ORA-01830 / ORA-01843 / ORA-01858 / ORA-01861date format errorsDate text does not match the formatUse TO_DATE with a matching format or ANSI literals
ORA-01839date not valid for month specified31 February via + INTERVAL MONTHUse ADD_MONTHS
ORA-01950no privileges on tablespaceNo quotaALTER USER ... QUOTA
ORA-02260 / ORA-00955table can have only one primary key / name already usedObject existsChoose another name or DROP first
ORA-02270 / ORA-02298no matching unique or primary key / cannot validate parent keyForeign key problemCreate the parent key; fix the data
ORA-02290check constraint violatedValue fails the ruleCorrect the data
ORA-02291integrity constraint violated - parent key not foundChild row without parentInsert the parent first
ORA-02292integrity constraint violated - child record foundParent with childrenDelete children, or use CASCADE
ORA-02449unique/primary keys referenced by foreign keysDROP TABLE of a parentCASCADE CONSTRAINTS
ORA-08002 / ORA-08004CURRVAL not defined / sequence exceeds MAXVALUECURRVAL before NEXTVAL / sequence exhaustedCall NEXTVAL; ALTER the sequence
ORA-12541 / ORA-12514no listener / service not knownDatabase down or wrong service nameStart it; use FREEPDB1
ORA-25154column part of USING clause cannot have qualifierQualified a USING / NATURAL join columnRemove the qualifier
ORA-30926unable to get a stable set of rowsMERGE source matches a target row twiceMake the ON condition unique
ORA-30483window functions are not allowed hereAnalytic function in WHEREUse an inline view
ORA-01031insufficient privilegesMissing system or object privilegeGRANT it
ORA-01720grant option does not existGranting a view over objects you hold without GRANT OPTIONOwner grants WITH GRANT OPTION

Appendix E: Glossary of Oracle and SQL Terms

Topics in this chapter

  • E.1 Database and Architecture
  • E.2 Relational Concepts
  • E.3 SQL Language
  • E.4 Transactions and Objects
  • E.5 Security
  • E.6 Performance and Time

E.1 Database and Architecture

TermMeaning
DatabaseThe files that store data: datafiles, control files, redo logs
InstanceMemory structures plus background processes that operate a database
SGA / PGAShared / private memory areas of the instance and of one server process
Buffer cachePart of the SGA that holds data blocks
Shared poolPart of the SGA that holds parsed SQL, plans and dictionary data
Redo / UndoRecords of changes for recovery / before-images for rollback and read consistency
SCNSystem change number: Oracle’s logical clock
CDB / PDBContainer database / pluggable database inside it
ListenerProcess that accepts client connections (default port 1521)
Service name / SIDName clients use to connect / identifier of an instance
Tablespace / datafile / segment / extent / blockLogical storage container / OS file / storage of one object / contiguous blocks / smallest I/O unit
SchemaThe objects owned by one user
Data dictionaryRead-only metadata views describing the database

E.2 Relational Concepts

TermMeaning
Relation, tuple, attributeTable, row, column
Primary keyUnique, not-null identifier of a row
Unique keyUnique value(s); NULL allowed
Foreign keyColumn(s) referencing a parent key; enforces referential integrity
Composite keyA key of several columns
Surrogate / natural keyGenerated meaningless key / key with business meaning
CardinalityNumber of rows; or the 1:N relationship between tables
NormalisationOrganising data to remove redundancy (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)
ERDEntity-relationship diagram
NULLAbsence of a value; comparisons with it are UNKNOWN
ConstraintA rule enforced by the database (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, CHECK)

E.3 SQL Language

TermMeaning
DQL / DML / DDL / DCL / TCLQuery / manipulation / definition / control / transaction control statements
AliasA temporary name for a column or table in one statement
PredicateA condition that is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN
JoinCombining rows of tables by a condition (inner, outer, self, cross, natural)
Cartesian productEvery row paired with every row; a join without a condition
Anti-join / semi-joinRows with no match / with at least one match (NOT EXISTS / EXISTS)
SubqueryA query nested inside another statement
Correlated subqueryA subquery that refers to the outer row
Inline viewA subquery in the FROM clause
Set operatorUNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, MINUS
Group functionAggregate over many rows (COUNT, SUM, AVG ...)
Analytic functionAggregate over a window that keeps every row
PseudocolumnA value that behaves like a column: ROWID, ROWNUM, LEVEL, NEXTVAL, CURRVAL
Substitution variableClient-side placeholder &x / &&x
Bind variableServer-side placeholder :x supplied at execution
CTASCREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT
CTE / WITH clauseA named subquery defined before the main query

E.4 Transactions and Objects

TermMeaning
TransactionA unit of work ended by COMMIT or ROLLBACK
ACIDAtomicity, consistency, isolation, durability
SavepointA marker inside a transaction to roll back to
Implicit commitThe commit that DDL, DCL and a normal exit perform
Read consistencyEach query sees a snapshot of committed data
LockProtection of a row or object during a change
DeadlockTwo sessions each waiting for a lock the other holds
IndexStructure that speeds up access to rows
SequenceGenerator of unique numbers
SynonymAn alias for an object
ViewA stored query
Materialized viewA view whose result is stored and refreshed
Identity columnA column filled by an internal sequence
Virtual columnA column computed from other columns, not stored
Temporary tableA table whose rows are private to a session or transaction
External tableA read-only table over a file outside the database
Recycle binWhere dropped tables wait to be restored or purged

E.5 Security

TermMeaning
UserAn account that owns a schema
System privilegeThe right to perform a kind of action in the database
Object privilegeThe right to act on one specific object
RoleA named group of privileges
GRANT OPTION / ADMIN OPTIONRight to pass on an object privilege / a system privilege or role
QuotaSpace a user may use in a tablespace

E.6 Performance and Time

TermMeaning
OptimizerComponent that chooses the execution plan
Execution planThe steps Oracle takes to run a statement
StatisticsData about tables and columns used by the optimizer
Hard / soft parseCompiling a new statement / reusing a cached one
Full table scan / index scanReading all blocks / reading through an index
Partition pruningReading only the partitions a query needs
Star schemaA fact table surrounded by dimension tables (SH)
Fact / dimension tableMeasures (SALES) / descriptive attributes (TIMES, PRODUCTS)
Database / session time zoneZone of the database / of one connection
IntervalA length of time: year-to-month or day-to-second
Hierarchical queryA query that walks a tree with START WITH / CONNECT BY

Appendix F: The Lab Test Kit — Verifying the Whole Lab

One script checks that HR, CO and SH are installed correctly and that the objects you built in the labs exist. It prints PASS when a value equals what Oracle’s installers report, WARN when the object exists but the number differs (a different release of the sample data, or you changed it), and FAIL when it is missing or empty. Save it as labs/lab_test_kit.sql and run it as SYSTEM.

-- lab_test_kit.sql : run as SYSTEM in FREEPDB1.   SET FEEDBACK OFF for a clean reportSET LINESIZE 120 PAGESIZE 100 FEEDBACK OFFCOLUMN item FORMAT A34COLUMN result FORMAT A6 WITH checks AS (  -- HR : the row counts of Oracle's HR installer  SELECT 'HR.REGIONS'     AS item,   5 AS expected, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.regions)     AS actual FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.COUNTRIES',            25,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.countries)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.LOCATIONS',            23,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.locations)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.DEPARTMENTS',          27,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.departments)           FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.JOBS',                 19,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.jobs)                  FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.EMPLOYEES',           107,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.employees)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR.JOB_HISTORY',          10,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr.job_history)           FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'HR payroll (SUM salary)', 691416,        (SELECT SUM(salary) FROM hr.employees)          FROM dual UNION ALL  -- CO : the counts reported by the CO installer  SELECT 'CO.CUSTOMERS',           392,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.customers)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.STORES',               23,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.stores)                FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.PRODUCTS',             46,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.products)              FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.ORDERS',             1950,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.orders)                FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.SHIPMENTS',          1892,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.shipments)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.ORDER_ITEMS',        3914,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.order_items)           FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'CO.INVENTORY',           566,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM co.inventory)             FROM dual UNION ALL  -- SH : the big tables  SELECT 'SH.SALES',            918843,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sh.sales)                 FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'SH.CUSTOMERS',         55500,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sh.customers)             FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'SH.CHANNELS',              5,            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sh.channels)              FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'SH.TIMES (>0)',            1,            (SELECT LEAST(COUNT(*), 1) FROM sh.times)       FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'SH.PRODUCTS (>0)',         1,            (SELECT LEAST(COUNT(*), 1) FROM sh.products)    FROM dual UNION ALL  SELECT 'SH.COUNTRIES (>0)',        1,            (SELECT LEAST(COUNT(*), 1) FROM sh.countries)   FROM dual)SELECT item, expected, actual,       CASE WHEN actual = expected THEN 'PASS'            WHEN actual > 0        THEN 'WARN'            ELSE 'FAIL' END AS resultFROM   checks; -- structure: keys must exist (at least these numbers of primary / foreign keys)SELECT owner,       COUNT(CASE WHEN constraint_type = 'P' THEN 1 END) AS primary_keys,       COUNT(CASE WHEN constraint_type = 'R' THEN 1 END) AS foreign_keys,       CASE WHEN COUNT(CASE WHEN constraint_type = 'P' THEN 1 END) >= 6            THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS resultFROM   dba_constraintsWHERE  owner IN ('HR','CO','SH')GROUP  BY owner ORDER BY owner; -- accounts and the project objects (WARN until you have done those chapters)SELECT username AS item,       CASE WHEN account_status = 'OPEN' THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS resultFROM   dba_users WHERE username IN CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'WARN' END AS resultFROM   dba_tables WHERE owner = 'CO' AND table_name = 'LAB_ORDERS'; SELECT 'EI_KPI_V in INSIGHT' AS item,       CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'WARN' END AS resultFROM   dba_views WHERE owner = 'INSIGHT' AND view_name = 'EI_KPI_V'; SET FEEDBACK ON

Topics in this chapter

  • F.1 Reading the Report

F.1 Reading the Report

ResultMeaningWhat to do
PASSThe object exists and the count matches Oracle’s installer outputNothing
WARNThe object exists but the number differs, or a project object is not created yetIf it is a sample table, a newer script release may differ slightly: check against the installer’s own verification table. If it is a project object, do the chapter that creates it
FAILThe object or the data is missingReinstall that schema (Chapter 4) — overwrite answers YES
ORA-00942 while the script runsA whole schema is missingInstall it with its *_install.sql

Note: HR’s payroll total of 691416 and the counts of Chapter 4 are the figures used throughout the labs. The script was written from Oracle’s documentation and installer output; if your sample-schema release differs, WARN lines are expected and harmless.

Oracle SQL

From Beginner to Advanced SQL (Structured Query Language)

Complete Hands-on Project-based Learning with the a fictional project “Enterprise Insight Project”, compatible with Oracle AI Database 26ai Free Edition, using Oracle sample database schemas: HR, CO, SH

From Oracle database installation to advanced analytic SQL.

Every chapter builds on one running project, the Enterprise Insight Project, which uses only Oracle’s official sample schemas — HR (Human Resources), CO (Customer Orders) and SH (Sales History) — so each exercise leaves the lab in a known state for the next one.

Every exercise comes with a RESET block (to put the lab back exactly as it was) and a REPLAY block (to re-apply the work quickly), so you can experiment without fear.

All 16 official 1Z0-071 exam topics are covered, in a sequence that goes from total beginner to advanced.

How to use this tutorial

  • Open a folder in the left menu (Part › Chapter) and click a topic.
  • Every code box has a Copy button. It copies only the commands: prompts such as HR> and the grey result lines are skipped, so you can paste straight into SQLcl.
  • Do the topics in order: each chapter builds on the previous ones. Use the Mark as done button to track your progress.
